answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The basalt multiplier is published, charged in ivory, and reef lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2111 identities would post 3236 proofs and burn roughly 77 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
